title: Comparing Splice Pricing Plans and Credits
summary: Splice pricing tiers determine your monthly sample allowance and access to exclusive software rent-to-own plans. Compare these costs to your budget.
body_markdown:
## Splice is a credit-based subscription for music samples


### How the Splice credit system works


The platform operates on a recurring monthly fee that deposits a fixed number of credits into a user’s account. These credits are the internal currency for the ecosystem.


A single credit typically unlocks one "one-shot", which is a single hit like a snare drum. It can also unlock one "loop", which is a repeating melodic or rhythmic phrase.


When the billing cycle ends, **credits do not always roll over** indefinitely. A producer who does not spend their full balance essentially pays for assets they never receive.


### The credit rollover cap


While active subscribers benefit from rollover, Splice does not enforce a stated maximum credit limit based on the specific tier of the user's plan.


> A producer who does not spend their full balance essentially pays for assets they never receive.


This cap prevents users from accumulating thousands of credits over several years without spending them, effectively placing a ceiling on the value an account can hold.


Once a user reaches their plan's maximum capacity, any new credits they pay for in the next billing cycle are forfeited if the balance is not reduced.


This creates a pressure to spend credits even during creative droughts to avoid losing the financial value of the subscription.


For those managing high-volume production schedules, a workflow built on Activepieces can automate the organization of these downloaded files into cloud storage.


The run is the meter, so a ten-step process that sorts, tags, and backs up a sample costs the same single credit to run as the two-step workaround it replaced.


Activepieces bills 1 credit per flow run regardless of the number of steps, a direct contrast to the **per-task or per-module metering** found on the Zapier or Make pricing pages.


### Splice Sounds vs Gear subscription plans


Splice separates its offerings into two distinct financial tracks: the Sounds plan, which covers the library of audio files, and the Gear plan, which facilitates "Rent-to-Own" agreements for professional software.


The Sounds subscription is a perpetual overhead cost. Gear payments function as installments toward the full retail price of a third-party plugin, such as the wavetable synthesizer Serum or the vocal processing suite Izotope Nectar.


Because of this distinction, a user can own their software tools outright after a set number of months, but they will never "own" the library itself. They own the specific samples they spent credits on, regardless of whether their subscription remains active.


### What happens to your samples if you cancel?


**Because unused credits always roll over to the next month while a plan stays active, there is no "use it or lose it" pressure forcing a producer to spend their entire bank before the billing period ends.** If a user terminates their subscription, they retain the legal right to use any samples they have already downloaded in their commercial projects.


They immediately lose access to any unspent credits remaining in their balance.


By restricting the ability to search the library and re-download previously owned sounds, Splice forces users to manually back up their local library to avoid losing access to their curated palette.


**32% of Hip-Hop** , 24% of R&B, and 4% of Rock songs in the Top 100 contain samples, according to Statista, suggesting that genre-specific production techniques heavily influence how artists approach modern composition.


As these genres continue to dominate the charts, the pressure to maintain a library subscription becomes a fixed cost of business for professional creators.


### Which Splice plan fits you


- The Sounds+ plan ($12.99/month) provides 100 credits for hobbyists building one or two tracks a month, effectively capping the creative scope of any single composition, which means users must carefully ration their assets to finish a project.
- The Creator plan ($19.99/month) offers 200 credits and access to "Beatmaker" tools for professional beatmakers who need a higher volume of loops for daily composition, so those working on a tight schedule can maintain a consistent production pace.
- The Creator+ plan ($39.99/month) grants 500 credits for studio teams in high-output environments where multiple projects run simultaneously, ensuring that collaborators do not exhaust their shared resources before the workday ends.
